tools.name: verify_text
tools.description: Scan HLA typing report text, or model output about HLA, for allele-shaped tokens and classify each one: valid / legacy (with modern form) / deleted (with successor) / fabricated. tools.name: normalize_allele
tools.description: Normalize one reported HLA allele name (any era) to current 2-field form, with G group, P group, serologic equivalent, and flags.

tools.name: allele_info
tools.description: Look up one exact name in the pinned release and return what it is: assigned (G/P group, first release, confirmed status, WMDA serology, null flag), valid_prefix (member count and sample), or deleted (successor). Not found if the name has never existed in any release.

tools.name: match_score
tools.description: Count a donor-recipient HLA match by the published counting rules (R1-R6): allele arithmetic over chromosomes, not a donor recommendation. recipient/donor: {"A": ["A*01:01","A*02:01"], "B": [...], ...} (two reported alleles per locus, any nomenclature era; allele strings only, no patient identifiers

tools.name: check_typing
tools.description: QC-check one HLA typing (all loci) against the pinned release: resolves every reported allele, flags unresolvable/outdated/locus-mismatched/null alleles, flags too-many/single/homozygous per locus, computes the B-leader (-21 M/T) and KIR-ligand (C1/C2/Bw4) profile, and DRB3/4/5 expected-vs-reported.

tools.name: donor_compat
tools.description: Donor/recipient immunogenetic compatibility under two published rule sets: HLA-B leader match (-21 M/T, Petersdorf 2020) for a single HLA-B mismatch, and KIR ligand (C1/C2/Bw4) class comparison, computed over each side's full typing QC. tools.name: about
tools.description: What this server is and is not, what to send it, benchmark evidence for why to use it, the beta state, and terms.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "beta_signup" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Put a user on the free public beta's notification list for paid API keys. Ask before calling: it records the address they give you. Re-signing the same address …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: beta_signup · Private data: verify_text, validate_gl_string, beta_signup · Public sink: verify_text, validate_gl_string, beta_signup, about.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: beta_signup · Private data: verify_text, validate_gl_string, beta_signup · Public sink: verify_text, validate_gl_string, beta_signup, about

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
